label: copy-phase input f fed back (from original position >= 2)
explanation: Token detector for the letter f, but only during the copy phase: it fires when the model's own fed-back output f arrives as input (in_tok == f, t > L), for f that sat at original position >= 2 (recall_idx >= 3). It essentially never fires on f in the original phase (219 of 57k activations) or on any other token. Firing is weak or absent when the fed-back f came from original position 0-1 (recall_idx 1-2): rate is 0.6% at recall_idx 2 versus about 3.3% (near-saturated for f) at recall_idx >= 3. Where f is at original position 2, firing depends on the sequence: long sequences (L = 8-9, many outputs still to go) often give false positives, while short sequences (L = 4) sometimes give weak activations at position 1. The strongest activations (near max) are on f fed back from mid or late original positions (about 4-7). When f appears twice, both occurrences usually fire, and the later one fires more strongly.

issues: The core claim holds. The feature is a detector for f fed back during the copy phase: in_tok f accounts for 100% of activation mass, the copy phase also accounts for 100%, and the original phase has only 219 of 57k activations. The original predicate reproduces on test (P 0.948, R 0.947, F1 0.948, mass recall 0.982).

The fixed cutoff recall_idx >= 3 is wrong at the edges, and the error depends systematically on L. Firing precision for f at recall_idx 2 (original position 1) by L: L=3 0.998, L=4 0.929, L=5 0.032, L=6 to 9 0.000. So for L = 3-4, f at position 1 fires almost every time, at full strength. Calling these 'some weak misses' undersells them: the test misses list shows them at 0.11 to 0.37 of max, and they are a whole class of activations the predicate leaves out.

Firing precision at recall_idx 3 (original position 2) falls as L grows: L=4-5 1.00, L=6 0.985, L=7 0.79, L=8 0.54, L=9 0.60. The false positives in the test misses list are all of this kind (f at position 2 with L = 7-9). They are a systematic class, not scattered noise.

Taken together, the gate tracks something like 'enough copy steps passed or close to the end' rather than a fixed original position. At recall_idx 2 it fires only when to_go <= 1. Adding that rule takes test recall from 0.947 to 0.993 and mass recall from 0.982 to 0.9995.
Minor inconsistency: the explanation says 'errors sit at the boundary, original position 2', but the misses are at original position 1 (recall_idx 2). Only the false positives are at position 2.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input f fed back, except early copies (f from original position 1 fires only when it is the last or second-to-last output; f from position 2 fires unreliably when L >= 8)
